title: Instagram and Aesthetic Dentistry: A Study of Content and Engagement Among Arabic Posts Related to Dental Smile
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 150 Instagram posts under 15 Arabic aesthetic-dentistry hashtags, reporting that 84.0% (126/150) were 'non-factual' — a share of items with an explicit denominator, which the paper itself presents as misinformation prevalence. HOWEVER the measure is typed QUALITY, not CONTENT: the numerator is defined as 'non-facts AND falsified information' and the positive category requires claims to be 'objectively true, RELEVANT, and minimal facts', so a wholly true — or claim-free promotional — post is scored non-factual. Per §3 the row is kept but excluded from prevalence. AN ADJUDICATOR SHOULD NOTE: if that reading stands, this is a QUALITY-ONLY study and §1 would screen it EXCLUDE; I have screened INCLUDE so the row and its reasoning are preserved rather than lost.

estimates.country: Not stated — Arabic-language hashtags, no geographic restriction (authors based in Saudi Arabia; framing is 'Arab countries')
estimates.measure_type: % of Instagram posts under Arabic aesthetic-dentistry hashtags whose claims were rated non-factual
estimates.denominator: 150 publicly available Instagram posts — the top 10 posts for each of 15 popular Arabic hashtags on smile alteration and Hollywood smiles, retrieved on a single day (4 February 2024) from a fresh, de-personalised account
estimates.definition: Claim accuracy rated on a simplified 2-point scale as 'non-factual', a category expressly covering both non-facts (absence of factual content) and falsified information; the positive category 'factual' required claims to be objectively true, relevant, and minimal facts
estimates.misinfo_def: “Claim accuracy was categorized as factual (objectively true, relevant, and minimal facts) or non-factual (including both non-facts and falsified information).”
estimates.source_quote: The accuracy of the claims made in these posts raises some concerns. Only 16.0% of the posts contain factual information, while the remaining 84.0% consist of non-factual claims.
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 137; Table 1 ('Accuracy of claims: Facts 24 (16.0) / Non-facts 126 (84.0)'); also Abstract
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two calibrated researchers (MA & JA) independently reviewed the posts after a pilot calibration exercise, disagreements resolved by discussion; claim accuracy specifically was then 'revised and confirmed' by a SINGLE experienced researcher (RA). No kappa or agreement statistic is reported for accuracy, no external ground truth (no guideline, evidence base or expert panel) is named, and the only instrument description is 'a simplified 2-point scale' adapted from a prior orthodontic-products study (ref 11).
estimates.moderator_quote: A comprehensive list of the top 10 posts for each selected hashtag was collected on the 4th of Feb 2024. Then, two calibrated researchers (MA & JA) independently reviewed the posts and collected the data. ... After data were collected and classified, one experienced researcher (RA) revised and confirmed the accuracy of claims (factual vs non-factual). ... To assess claim accuracy for each post, a simplified 2-point scale was adopted.
estimates.notes: THE KEY JUDGEMENT CALL. Typed QUALITY rather than CONTENT for three reasons: (i) the numerator explicitly pools 'non-facts' (no factual content) with 'falsified information', so absence of a claim counts the same as a false claim; (ii) 69.3% of the corpus is marketing/promotional posts and 43.3% are practice advertisements — items that typically make no verifiable claim at all yet are scored non-factual (Table 2: 97/104 marketing posts, 93.3%, were 'non-facts'); (iii) the positive category adds a RELEVANCE condition ('objectively true, relevant, and minimal facts'), so a true but off-topic post fails. A wholly true item can therefore receive the label, which §3 sends to QUALITY. within_misinfo_content is set true only as a belt-and-braces flag that this value must not enter a prevalence pool; the denominator is not a misinformation-only sample. breadth is '' per the schema rule for QUALITY. country_norm=Global because the corpus is defined by LANGUAGE (Arabic hashtags) with no geographic filter, even though the authors and framing are Saudi/Arab. population_scope='other' because the posters are a mix of patients (49.3%), dentists (32.7%) and dental-related groups/practices (18.0%) rather than a general public. denom_selection=curated: top-10-per-hashtag is a rank-truncated set. The value itself is verbatim and internally consistent with Table 1 (24 + 126 = 150); confidence is medium because of the construct call and the paper's poor internal consistency (see missed_or_uncertain).

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Sub-group non-factual rates stated verbatim in the Discussion but not extracted per R4 (they are subdivisions of the single 84.0% estimate, and inherit the same QUALITY problem): by theme — marketing 93.3% and sharing-experience 95.7% non-factual, informative/educational 69.6% factual; by poster role — patients and dental-related groups 96% non-factual vs dentists 61.2%; by post type — concern/procedure discussions 62.5% factual (Table 4). Table 2 and Table 3 report the same data as COLUMN percentages of the 126 non-facts (marketing 77.0%, sharing experience 17.5%, informative 5.6%; patients 56.3%, groups 19.8%, dentists 23.8%), which are easy to misread as prevalence rates — they are not. (2) INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES an adjudicator should see: the Discussion says 'out of 150 Instagram posts, only 17% contain factual information' where the Results and Table 1 say 16.0%; the Methods state posts 'in languages other than Arabic were eliminated' yet Table 1 records 13 English-only and 9 'other'-language posts (only 100/150 are Arabic-only); the Discussion says 'marketing accounts use photos most frequently (62.5%)' where Table 2 gives 84.4%, and quotes reel figures (47.8%, 60.9%) that do not appear in Table 2. None of these affect the extracted 84.0% but they lower confidence in the paper generally. (3) Figures quoted from other studies and barred by R8: 'a violation of the dental code was as high as 43.75% and 46.9%' (ref 10) and 'increased demand for dental cosmetic procedures among patients in Arab countries (49.3%)' (ref 9). (4) All engagement metrics (likes, comments, followers, hashtags, watermarks 74.0%) are not misinformation measures. (5) No exposure, reach, sharing or concentration measure exists in this paper.

rob.design: Cross-sectional observational content analysis of publicly available Instagram posts. Frame: 15 popular Arabic hashtags on smile alteration/Hollywood smile, chosen after exploring popular terms plus a pilot calibration; top 10 posts per hashtag retrieved on a single day, 4 February 2024, from a newly created account with no prior Instagram association (GPS disabled, suggested posts snoozed, sensitive-content control set to 'More') to limit algorithmic personalisation — a genuine methodological strength. n=150; non-related, duplicate and non-Arabic posts stated to be removed (contradicted by Table 1's language distribution). Two calibrated researchers coded independently with consensus resolution, but the accuracy variable was finally adjudicated by a single researcher and NO inter-rater reliability statistic is reported for it. No external ground truth or accuracy criteria are specified. Single time point, single platform, no sample-size justification, no audience data (authors' own stated limitation).
